Meta last year launched a school partner programme for Instagram, pledging to prioritise cyberbullying reports submitted by students.

The company has now expanded the programme to allow schools to post Stories and notes viewable only by their students, with support for clubs, teams and more…

Instagram School Partners Programme

Instagram does not have a great track record when it comes to teen mental health. Internal research at the company suggests Instagram may negatively affect as many as one in five teen girls, increasing anxiety around issues like physical attractiveness and popularity.

Cyberbullying has been a significant problem for teen social media users, and Meta launched a programme last year to help schools deal with the issue. When a school signs up for its partner programme, Meta pledges to prioritise reports submitted by students and staff.

New School Features

Meta says it is adding a number of features to the programme today.

Channels. Allow schools to share updates with parents and students, with only school admins able to post in the channel.

School Stories and Notes. Staff and students can both post, with content only displayed to verified students at that school. School admins can delete posts.

Clubs and Teams. Anyone at the school can create clubs and teams, which serve as a centralised location for posting related events and information.

Student Directory. Students can look up other students at their school on the platform, with information only displayed to other students and teen followers who follow each other.

Meta says the new features are designed to be used outside of classroom hours, noting that parents can use teen account settings to block the platform during school hours.

High school student verification is handled by UNiDAYS, the same company that provides education pricing verification for Apple.
